original_value: AbstractWe introduce a modal separation logic MSL whose models are memory states from separation logic and the logical connectives include modal operators as well as separating conjunction and implication from separation logic. With such a combination of operators, some fragments of MSL can be seen as genuine modal logics whereas some others capture standard separation logics, leading to an original language to speak about memory states. We analyse the decidability status and the computational complexity of several fragments of MSL, obtaining surprising results by design of proof methods that take into account the modal and separation features of MSL. For example, the satisfiability problem for the fragment of MSL with $\Diamond $, the difference modality $\langle \neq \rangle $ and separating conjunction $\ast $ is shown Tower-complete whereas the restriction either to $\Diamond $ and $\ast $ or to $\langle \neq \rangle $ and $\ast $ is only NP-complete. We establish that the full logic MSL admits an undecidable satisfiability problem. Furthermore, we investigate variants of MSL with alternative semantics and we build bridges with interval temporal logics and with logics equipped with sabotage operators.

result.paraphrase: We introduce modal separation logic MSL, whose semantics uses the memory states of separation logic and whose language combines modal operators with the separating conjunction and implication of separation logic. This mix yields an original way to reason about memory states: some fragments of MSL behave as true modal logics, while others recover standard separation logics. We study decidability and computational complexity for several MSL fragments and obtain surprising results by developing proof techniques that exploit both the modal and separation aspects of MSL. For instance, satisfiability for the fragment containing $\Diamond$, the difference modality $\langle \neq \rangle$, and separating conjunction $\ast$ is Tower-complete, whereas the restrictions to either $\Diamond$ and $\ast$ or $\langle \neq \rangle$ and $\ast$ are only NP-complete. We also prove that the full MSL has an undecidable satisfiability problem. In addition, we examine variants of MSL under alternative semantics and connect them with interval temporal logics and logics featuring sabotage operators.
